extracted.intended_audience: TeX / plain-TeX users and macro programmers (advanced users, typesetters, macro authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for writing plain-TeX macros and for typesetting with TeX (behavior of tokens, boxes, glue, line/page breaking, catcodes, math typesetting, etc.). Intended to help macro writers and advanced users avoid pitfalls and produce correct output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow a space before a dash macro
rubrics_metrics.description: The \unskip allows people to leave a space before typing \dash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \unskip in macro definitions that should allow a user to type a space before invoking a punctuation macro like \dash; \extraspace can be used as a precaution for the following word.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on control-sequence interpretation while scanning arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX doesn't interpret control sequences when it scans an argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A control sequence might define another control sequence before TeX is told to look at #1; don't expect TeX to expand/interpret control sequences during the scanning of an argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reserving backslash-like tokens for limited uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Reverse slashes (backslashes) are uncommon in formulas or text and it was felt best not to reserve \\ for such limited use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typists can define \\ to be whatever they want (including \backslash) if they need it; don't globally reserve rare sequences and break conventions unless necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for active-character dual behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Active characters (category 13) behave like control sequences in most cases but like character tokens in token lists of \uppercase or \lowercase and when unexpanded after \if or \ifcat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using active characters, remember they will act differently depending on context — you cannot assume purely 'control sequence' semantics everywhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catcode assignments are local and take effect immediately
rubrics_metrics.description: When a group ends the effects of all \catcode definitions within the group are wiped out except those that were \global; new category codes take effect as soon as a \catcode assignment has been digested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful with ordering and spacing when changing catcodes inside groups; TeX reads the token following a constant before evaluating that constant, so missing spaces can make catcode changes behave unexpectedly.

rubrics_metrics.name: To get a backslash from \string, make backslash active or adjust \escapechar
rubrics_metrics.description: To get \ from \string you need to make backslash an active character or change \escapechar (negative or >255) so that \string\\ works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One solution is to change the catcode of \\ to 13 (active) inside a local group and then use /message{/string\}; alternatively, set \escapechar appropriately. Beware of other side effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be careful using macros with \ifx and \csname inside conditionals
rubrics_metrics.description: A control sequence like \def\ifundefined#1{\expandafter\ifx\csname#1\endcsname\relax} must be used with care; it cannot be included in conditional text because the \ifx will not be seen when \ifundefined isn't expanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Macros that rely on expansion-sensitive primitives should be used only where their expansion timing is appropriate; avoid hiding such constructs inside unexpanded conditionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand expansion order with \uppercase and \expandafter
rubrics_metrics.description: First \uppercase produces :A\lowercase{BC} then you get :Abc; \expandafter expands the token after the control sequence, not the token after the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully plan the sequence of \uppercase, \lowercase, and \expandafter to achieve the intended expansion order; small reordering changes the result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escape characters of categories 0,1,5,9,14,15 when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: When a character is of category 0,1,5,9,14 or 15 the extra \ must be used; and the \ doesn't hurt, so you can always use it to be safe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because category code semantics differ, prefacing special characters with \ is a safe default to avoid them being treated as comment, space, or grouping characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different category codes produce different tokens
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters of category 5 might be converted into different tokens while category 14 never produces a token; control sequence names treat letters differently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't assume visually identical characters are identical to TeX; ensure you use the right category code for the intended token behavior (especially for dollar signs, percent signs, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \obeyspaces or make spaces active to display spaces in error contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: When TeX prints the context of an error message, some spaces may be ignored; if you had typed \obeyspaces you would have seen the space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need to preserve spaces in contexts like error messages or verbatim-like output, enable \obeyspaces or use active characters appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of how returns and category codes turn into tokens
rubrics_metrics.description: The final space comes from the (return) placed at the end of the line; code for hex/octal yields tokens depending on following characters and line-start state ignores initial spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line endings, returns, and numeric or hex notations affect the token stream; test edge cases to avoid surprises in tokenization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use braces to keep font changes local and to control accent scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The extra braces keep font changes local. An argument makes the use of \' more consistent with the use of other accents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enclose font or accent changes in braces to limit their scope and avoid unintended effects in surrounding text. When an accent primitive isn't available in a font, borrow an accent from another font and localize with braces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Borrow accents from other fonts when unavailable in current font
rubrics_metrics.description: The proper umlaut is \H which isn't available in \tt, so it's necessary to borrow the accent from another font; e.g. use {	t P\'al Erd{\bf\H{\tt o}}s} to get a suitably dark accent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a desired accent doesn't exist in the current typewriter or monospaced font, combine fonts locally to obtain the accent, ensuring visual consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only one magnification per job; font availability matters
rubrics_metrics.description: There can be at most one magnification per job. Three separate runs are needed to use multiple magnifications, and the output may look funny if the fonts don't exist at the stated magnifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \magnification once per run and run TeX multiple times for different magnifications; ensure the required fonts exist at those magnifications or expect fallback/funny output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnification factor is 1.2 per magstep
rubrics_metrics.description: Magnification is by a factor of 1.2. For example, \magstep1 means multiply point size by 1.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute final font sizes by applying 1.2^n for \magstep n; be mindful that magnification changes point sizes of fonts and may affect layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspect boxes with \setbox and \showbox to understand internals
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \setbox0=\hbox{...} and \showbox0 to reveal implementation details (e.g., italic correction is implemented by placing a kern after the character).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment with \setbox and \showbox to inspect heights, depths, shifts, and inserted kerns; TeX internal calculations use sp units and rounding may produce unexpected tiny differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box dimensions are just large enough to enclose contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The height, depth, and width of the enclosing box should be just large enough to enclose all of the contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect boxes to be tight around content unless you explicitly add glue/kern; use measured box dimensions when aligning or composing boxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: When constructing hbox macros usable at paragraph start, avoid forcing unwanted indentation
rubrics_metrics.description: To make a macro that expands to an hbox usable both mid-paragraph and at the beginning, use \unskip\hbox{...} or better, use \leavevmode which solves this efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define macros that begin horizontal mode with \leavevmode (which is \unhbox\voidbox) so users don't need to type \indent and you don't insert unwanted indentation at paragraph start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blank spaces are ignored in math formulas and vertical modes
rubrics_metrics.description: Blank spaces at the ends of lines are ignored in math formulas and in vertical modes; only the first of several such spaces might have any effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on literal spaces for separation in math mode; use explicit spacing commands when necessary. Be aware that multiple blank tokens may be collapsed or ignored depending on mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect TeX's mode nesting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertical mode can occur only as the outermost mode; horizontal and display math modes must be immediately enclosed by vertical or internal vertical mode; ordinary math mode cannot be immediately enclosed by vertical or internal vertical mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing macros or selecting where to begin displays/math, ensure proper nesting of modes to avoid errors and unexpected behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \nobreak in math to prevent unwanted breaks without adding unwanted glue
rubrics_metrics.description: \hbox{$x=0$} is unbreakable and ${x=0}$ cannot be broken; a third solution $x=\nobreak0$ avoids both defects (prevents break and avoids extra space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer $x=\nobreak0$ to keep relation spacing correct and to avoid inserting fixed glue from an \hbox that might add unwanted blank at line edges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit hyphenation breaks with high penalty values
rubrics_metrics.description: \exhyphenpenalty=10000 prohibits breaks after explicit hyphens; similarly \hyphenpenalty=10000 prevents breaks after implicit discretionary hyphens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set these penalties to 10000 to completely prevent hyphenation at those spots; use with care as it can lead to overfull boxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define forced breaks with a penalty of -10000 and know penalty combination rules
rubrics_metrics.description: \def\break{\penalty-10000} creates a forced break; \break cannot be cancelled by another penalty. When two penalties occur in a row, their combined effect is the minimum of the two unless both force breaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that penalties combine by min (except forced breaks). Avoid unnecessary subtraction of large constants in penalties as it may cause arithmetic overflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid subtracting large constants to manipulate penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no point in subtracting a large constant whose effect on the total demerits is known a priori, especially when that might cause arithmetic overflow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use documented penalty mechanisms rather than arithmetic tricks; rely on documented demerit and penalty semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \parfillskip=\parindent to get symmetric paragraph filling
rubrics_metrics.description: Just say \parfillskip=\parindent. TeX will not be able to find appropriate line breaks unless each paragraph is sufficiently long, but with appropriate text the output will be symmetrically balanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting \parfillskip allows you to control how the last line fills; use it for centered-looking paragraphs but ensure paragraphs are long enough for the algorithm to find breaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer changing \linepenalty to forcing loose paragraphs rather than nontzero looseness
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting nontzero looseness makes TeX work harder; achieve almost the same result more efficiently by setting \linepenalty=100 instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want to encourage different line breaking without expensive computation, tweak \linepenalty rather than relying on \looseness adjustments that raise computation cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \null or \hbox{...} to prevent hyphenation and to control spacing of acronyms
rubrics_metrics.description: To typeset an unbreakable short acronym like NASA, use \hbox{NASA} or NASA\null (\null is \hbox{}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a zero-width box (\null) to keep text together or to prevent undesirable breaks without inserting visible space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use grouping to confine temporary dimension changes and restore \hsize appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: When changing \hsize or \rightskip for one paragraph, change it back at the end; one method avoids grouping by redefining \par to restore \hsize after the paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that changes to page shape or skips are properly restored (either by grouping or by redefining \par) so subsequent paragraphs are unaffected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribute infinite stretchability carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Infinite stretchability cancels out finite stretchability in a line; in some cases infinite glue results in text being moved far beyond the right edge of the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using infinite glue casually; understand that infinite glue overrides finite flexibility and can produce unintended placements. If you want evenly spread space, use \spaceskip to increase the amount of finite stretchability between words.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX prefers one very bad line over multiple moderately bad lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Distributing extra space evenly could lead to several lines of maximum badness; it's better to have just one bad line rather than three bad lines because TeX doesn't distinguish degrees when lines are really awful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you truly want to spread space evenly, set \spaceskip. Otherwise accept TeX's preference for minimizing the number of very bad lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: To insert marginal symbols or hanging markers, use \vadjust with struts
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid opening up the paragraph height, use \strut and \vadjust{\kern-\strutdepth\specialstar} where \specialstar is a vbox of height 0 and depth \strutdepth that places a marker in the margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct marginal marks using \vadjust and struts so you don't change line heights; assume the containing line's depth does not exceed \dp\strutbox.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insert bullets by setting \everypar appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Define \def\insertbullets{\everypar={\llap{$\bullet$\enspace}}} to insert a bullet at start of each paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using \everypar is a simple device to add consistent left-inserted material (bullets, hanging indentation, numbers), but beware of interactions with paragraph shape and other \everypar uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displays begun with $$ vs \noindent$$ behave differently re indentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting a paragraph with $$ instead of with \noindent$$ causes TeX to insert a paragraph indentation that will appear on a line by itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \noindent before display math if you do not want a paragraph indentation line preceding the display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page-breaking constraints: at least one box per page absent insertions; watch top/bottom box limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A page always contains at least one box if there are no insertions. Statement (a) fails if the height of the topmost box exceeds 10pt; statement (b) fails if the depth of the bottommost box exceeds 2.2pt or glue/kern comes between the bottommost box and the page break unless it cancels the depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing page content with top/bottom boxes and insertions, ensure boxes and insertions respect TeX's page-breaking thresholds and that you don't inadvertently create impossible breakpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid placing \vadjust{\eject} on same line as a footnote
rubrics_metrics.description: If \vadjust{\eject} occurs on the same line as a footnote then that footnote may be forcibly detached; other \vadjust commands on that line could interpose breakpoints before the insertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not place forced page-ejects via \vadjust on the same line as footnotes or other insertions to avoid undesirable detachment or ordering issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: In math mode, keep punctuation out of formulas and manage spaces carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Spaces disappear between dollar signs; punctuation that belongs to a sentence should not be included in a formula. Also, leave a space after control words like \If when needed (e.g., Ifx = ... caused by forgetting a space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write punctuation outside $...$ when it belongs to the sentence; ensure proper spacing after control words and be careful with spaces around dollar signs to avoid concatenation errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brace superscripts/subscripts and be explicit with grouping in math
rubrics_metrics.description: Superscripts and subscripts can be given in either order but you should not leave out any of the braces shown; additional braces around letters or numbers are harmless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include braces where indicated in examples to avoid surprises (e.g., $10..10$ would be wrong); use extra braces if it clarifies grouping or prevents misparsing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \mathcode changes sparingly and confine them to limited scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Changing \mathcode, e.g., making '.' act like \cdot by \mathcode'.=11 0201, could be dangerous since ordinary periods are used frequently in displayed equations; the \mathcode change should be confined to places where every period is to be a \cdot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When altering token classifications such as \mathcode, localize changes with grouping or macros to avoid widespread unintended consequences in mathematics and text.
